title: The Rolling Stones Tie The Beatles at No. 2 on U.K. Albums Chart’s Leaderboard With 15th No. 1 LP
summary: The group earned its first U.K. chart-topping record in 1964.
contentText:
The Rolling Stones has earned its 15th No. 1 on the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart dated July 17 with Foreign Tongues .

Related

The legendary rockers and current Billboard cover stars are now joint-second on the all-time rankings, tied with The Beatles , though Paul McCartney plays bass on Foreign Tongues ’ cut “Covered In You.”

Both groups trail Robbie Williams who took the top spot in January with his Britpop , his 16th overall. The Stones were previously tied in third position with Taylor Swift at 14 each.

The band last hit the No. 1 spot with 2023’s Hackney Diamonds , and first hit the top spot in 1964 with its self-titled debut LP.

In a wide-ranging conversation with Billboard ‘s Joe Lynch, Mick Jagger and Keith Richards discussed their thoughts on artificial intelligence, Olivia Rodrigo and the chances of heading out on the road in support of the new LP and more. (Read the full interview here .)

A reissue of My Chemical Romance’s 2010 LP Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys lands at No. 2 following the group’s run of U.K. shows. Over the weekend of July 8-11, the emo band performed at Wembley Stadium as part of an anniversary tour for its seminal 2006 album, The Black Parade .

Olivia Rodrigo holds her position week-on-week at No. 3 with her third LP, you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love , and Michael Jackson’s The Essential collection finishes at No. 4.

December 10’s On Your Side EP closes at No. 5 to give the boy band a strong start to its recording career; it’s the highest charting debut for a British boy band in six years following New Hope Club’s self-titled 2020 debut album (No. 5).

A 20th anniversary re-recording of Sheffield metallers Bring Me the Horizon’s debut LP Count Your Blessings I Repented lands at No. 6, an improvement of its original 2006 ranking at No. 93.

Future’s The Real Me lands at No. 27, while Jack White’s Frozen Charlotte closes at No. 29.
